section: Advent of Europeans - Portuguese, Dutch, English, French and Danish
subsections: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court
Indian rulers' dealings with the Portuguese

accepted.s: Who was the earliest English traveller to visit the Mughal court among the following?
accepted.x: Ralph Fitch visited the Mughal court in the 1580s during Akbar’s reign and is identified as an early English traveller.
accepted.tq: Use the direct name-and-period recall method.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s: Ralph Fitch visited the Mughal court during the reign of which Mughal emperor?
accepted.x: Ralph Fitch’s visit to the Mughal court in the 1580s took place during Akbar’s reign.
accepted.tq: Match the traveller with the contemporary ruler.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Captain William Hawkins reached the Mughal court in 1608–09.
2. He conducted the first English trade mission to the Mughal court.
3. His mission was refused under Portuguese pressure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Hawkins visited Jahangir’s court in 1608–09, led the first English trade mission there and faced Portuguese pressure resulting in refusal.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the traveller’s date, purpose and result.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s: With reference to Thomas Best, which one of the following is correct?
o: He represented the Danish Company at the court of Shah Jahan.
He defeated the Portuguese at Swally and obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
He was refused permission for trade under Portuguese pressure in 1608.
He secured the right to establish factories throughout the Mughal Empire in 1615.
accepted.x: Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally in 1612, and the English obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
accepted.tq: Separate closely associated English envoys by their specific achievement.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s: Sir Thomas Roe visited the court of which Mughal emperor as the envoy of James I?
accepted.x: Sir Thomas Roe was the envoy of James I and visited Jahangir’s court in 1615.
accepted.tq: Use the envoy–emperor association to eliminate adjacent Mughal reigns.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s: The principal result of Sir Thomas Roe’s mission to the Mughal court was that the English obtained the right to
o: establish factories across the Mughal Empire
exclude all European traders from Surat
accepted.x: Sir Thomas Roe’s mission in 1615 secured the right for the English to establish factories across the Mughal Empire.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical consequence of a diplomatic mission.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s: The farman issued by Farrukhsiyar in 1717 is associated with which concession to the English East India Company?
o: Transfer of Bombay at nominal rent
Permission to build a fort at Bhatkal
accepted.x: Farrukhsiyar’s farman of 1717 granted the English East India Company the privilege of duty-free trade in Bengal.
accepted.tq: Link the ruler and year with the precise commercial concession.
accepted.sec: English envoys and travellers at the Mughal court  [other exams]

accepted.s: Goa was taken by the Portuguese in 1510 from the
accepted.x: The Portuguese captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultan in 1510.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–territory trap used in medieval history questions.
accepted.sec: Indian rulers' dealings with the Portuguese  [other exams]

accepted.s: Diu was obtained by the Portuguese in 1535 from
accepted.x: The Portuguese acquired Diu from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1535.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Gujarat ruler from other Indian rulers associated with Portuguese settlements.
accepted.sec: Indian rulers' dealings with the Portuguese  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Portuguese obtained permission to build a fort at Bhatkal with the consent of
accepted.x: The Portuguese obtained Vijayanagara consent to build a fort at Bhatkal during the period of Krishnadevaraya, when horse trade was significant.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–fort-location association rather than the better-known Goa association.
accepted.sec: Indian rulers' dealings with the Portuguese  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Marathas took Salsette and Bassein.
B. Portuguese acquired Diu from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat.
C. Portuguese captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultan.
D. Shah Jahan expelled the Portuguese from Hooghly.
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Goa in 1510, Diu in 1535, expulsion from Hooghly in 1632, and the Maratha capture of Salsette and Bassein in 1739.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle dates.
accepted.sec: Indian rulers' dealings with the Portuguese  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Portuguese and Maratha relations?
o: The Marathas took Salsette and Bassein in 1739, while the Portuguese held Goa against them in 1798.
The Portuguese surrendered Goa to the Marathas in 1739.
The Portuguese took Salsette and Bassein from the Marathas in 1739.
The Marathas expelled the Portuguese from Goa in 1798.
accepted.x: The Marathas captured Salsette and Bassein in 1739, but the Portuguese continued to hold Goa against the Marathas in 1798.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between territories captured and territories retained by the Portuguese.
accepted.sec: Indian rulers' dealings with the Portuguese  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Battle of Swally, fought near Surat in 1612, was fought between the
accepted.x: At Swally in 1612, the English under Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese near Surat.
accepted.tq: Match the battle with its two European participants.

accepted.s: The Battle of Jask/Ormuz is correctly associated with which of the following?
o: English victory over the Portuguese in 1620/1622
English victory over the Dutch at Chinsura in 1759
French victory over the English at Wandiwash in 1760
accepted.x: The English fought the Portuguese at Jask in 1620 and Ormuz in 1622 and emerged victorious; Ormuz was taken for the Shah of Persia.
accepted.tq: Use the battle–year–participants combination to reject swapped European powers.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Colachel — Travancore and Dutch
2. Bedara — English and Dutch
3. Wandiwash — English and French
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Colachel was fought between Travancore and the Dutch, Bedara between the English and Dutch, and Wandiwash between the English and French.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure battle–participants pair and check the remaining pairs.

accepted.s: Who led the Travancore side in the Battle of Colachel against the Dutch in 1741?
accepted.x: Travancore, under Marthanda Varma, defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741.
accepted.tq: Avoid the ruler–commander swap by linking the regional ruler with the battle.

accepted.s: The Battle of Bedara, also known as the Battle of Chinsura, was fought in 1759 between the
accepted.x: At Bedara or Chinsura in 1759, the English under Clive defeated the Dutch, after which the Dutch shifted their attention to Indonesia.
accepted.tq: Test the alternative name and the participants together.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome of the Battle of Wandiwash?
o: The Dutch defeated Travancore under Marthanda Varma.
The English defeated the French under Eyre Coote.
The Portuguese defeated the English under Thomas Best.
The French defeated the English under Lally.
accepted.x: The English, led by Eyre Coote, defeated the French under Lally at Wandiwash in 1760.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly matched commander, opponents and outcome.

accepted.s: The Danish settlements of Serampore and Tranquebar were sold to the British in
accepted.x: The Danes sold Serampore and Tranquebar to the British in 1845.
accepted.tq: Use the date-range elimination method for a late colonial transaction.

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains an important reason for the ultimate success of the British in India?
o: The British relied exclusively on naval power and did not use Indian alliances.
The British avoided all involvement in the internal disputes of Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was a private joint-stock company with steady finance and exploited rivalries among Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was directly financed and administered by every Indian ruler.
accepted.x: The British benefited from the steady finances of a private joint-stock company and from using the rivalries among Indian rulers.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines both stated causal factors without an extreme claim.

accepted.s: Which development most directly marked the end of the Portuguese naval monopoly in the Indian Ocean?
o: The expulsion of the Portuguese from Hooghly by Shah Jahan alone
The rise of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers
The establishment of the French settlement at Yanam
The sale of Serampore and Tranquebar by the Danes
accepted.x: The Portuguese naval monopoly ended with the emergence of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers.
accepted.tq: Identify the broad historical significance rather than a single local event.

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets consists entirely of places associated with the Andhra angle of European trade?
accepted.x: Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nizampatnam and Bheemunipatnam are the Andhra-linked places listed in connection with European trade; Yanam is another such place.
accepted.tq: Use the regional grouping to eliminate places belonging to other European centres.

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with the Andhra region’s export trade under the European companies?
accepted.x: Andhra’s calico and Kalamkari were important articles connected with the region’s export trade.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the regional export products from commodities associated with other trade centres.

accepted.s: The term ‘Golden Farman’ is associated with the history of
o: European trade in the Andhra region
The Portuguese capture of Goa from Bijapur
accepted.x: The Golden Farman is listed as an Andhra-related aspect of the history of European trade.
accepted.tq: Recognise the regional keyword instead of substituting a better-known European event.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Portuguese presence in India is correct?
o: The Portuguese were the last Europeans to arrive and left India in 1845.
The Portuguese were the first to arrive but left India immediately after the capture of Goa in 1510.
The Portuguese came after the French and left India in 1798.
The Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India and were the last to leave in 1961.
accepted.x: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India and remained until 1961, making them the last European power to leave.
accepted.tq: Test the paired FIRST/LAST distinction and reject swapped chronology.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following battles in chronological order:
A. Battle of Colachel
B. Battle of Bedara
C. Battle of Swally
D. Battle of Wandiwash
accepted.x: The sequence is Swally (1612), Colachel (1741), Bedara (1759) and Wandiwash (1760).
accepted.tq: Place the earliest battle first and distinguish the closely spaced 1759–1760 events.
